## Introduction 

:::{.build}
👉 `Objective`: Model the copper concentration in MKF80 as a function of `TOC` (Total Organic Carbon) and `Oxygen` parameters.
:::

:::{.build}
👉 `Methods`: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Regression, Generalized Method of Moments (GMM), and Vector Autoregression (VAR).
:::

:::{.build}
👉 `Motivation`: 
:::

:::{.build}
- What is the Opportunity Cost of frequently performing the track removal process in the Electric Generator (depolarization)? 
:::

:::{.build}
- Is there effective control over this process?
:::

:::{.build}
- What can be done to minimize it?
:::

```{r gráficos-toc, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
    ))
  ) +
  
  labs(title = "Behavior of Copper, Oxygen, and TOC During the Study Period") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Ordinary Least Squares Model {.build}
```{r linear-model, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo = FALSE, fig.height=8, fig.width=10, out.width="100%"}
teste_modelo3 <- lm(Cu_MKF80 ~ TOC_80 + O2_80, data = mkf6)

resultados <- data.frame(
  Coeficiente = c("Intercept", "TOC", "Oxygen"),
  Estimativa = c(13.158571, 0.018444, -0.281026),
  "Standard Error" = c(3.061136, 0.00101, 0.150236),
  "t-value" = c(4.299, 18.12, -1.871),
  "p-value" = c("5.38e-05 *** ", "< 2e-16 *** ", "0.0655  .⚠️ ")
) 
kable(resultados, digits = 4, align = "c", caption = "OLS Model Results") %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("bordered"),
    full_width = TRUE, 
    position = c("center"),
    font_size = 19, 
    fixed_thead = TRUE) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, color = "gray1") %>%
  column_spec(2, bold = TRUE, color = "gray") %>% 
  column_spec(3, bold = TRUE, color = "gray") %>% 
  column_spec(4, bold = TRUE, color = "gray") %>% 
  column_spec(5, bold = TRUE, color = "gray") %>% 
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#404040")

```
Model Equation:

$$
Cu_t = 13.16 + 0.0184 \cdot TOC - 0.281 \cdot O_2 + \varepsilon_t
$$

## GMM Model with Instruments {.build}
```{r gmm-model, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo = FALSE, fig.height=8, fig.width=10, out.width="100%"}

mkf7 <- mkf6 %>%
  mutate(
    TOC_lag2 = lag(TOC_80, 2),
    O_2_lag7 = lag(O2_80, 7),
    Cu_lag2 = lag(Cu_MKF80, 2),
    TOC_MA6 = zoo::rollmean(TOC_80, 6, fill = NA),  # Média móvel
  ) %>% 
  na.omit()  # Remove linhas com NA (geradas pelas defasagens)
# Converter tibble para matriz (necessário para a função gmm)
dados_mat <- mkf7 %>% 
  drop_na()

dados_mat2 <- as.matrix(dados_mat)
# Error in theta[2] * TOC : argumento não-numérico para operador binário


# Função de Momento: resíduos x instrumentos
momentos <- function(theta, x) {
  Cu_MKF80 <- x[, "Cu_MKF80"]
  TOC_80 <- x[, "TOC_80"]
  O2_80 <- x[, "O2_80"]
  TOC_lag2 <- x[, "TOC_lag2"]
  O_2_lag7 <- x[, "O_2_lag7"]
  Cu_lag2 <- x[, "Cu_lag2"]
  TOC_MA6 <- x[, "TOC_MA6"]
  
  erro <- Cu_MKF80 - (theta[1] + theta[2] * TOC_80 + theta[3] * O2_80 + theta[4] * Cu_lag2) 
  
  # Condições de momento: E[erro * instrumentos] = 0
  return(cbind(
    erro,
    erro*x[,3],  # TOC_lag1
    erro*x[,4],  # O2_lag1
    erro*x[,5],  # TOC_lag2
    erro*x[,6],  # O2_lag2
    erro*x[,7],  # TOC_lag3
    erro*x[,8]   # Média móvel TOC
  ))
}

# Estimação GMM (two-step é mais eficiente)
modelo_gmm2 <- gmm(
  g = momentos,
  x = dados_mat,
  t0 = c(1.1, 1.1, 1.3, 1.1),         # Valores iniciais para beta0, beta1, beta2
  type = "twoStep",        # Estimação em dois estágios
  kernel = "Bartlett",     # Kernel para HAC
  bw = bwNeweyWest    # Função que calcula automaticamente
)

resultados <- data.frame(
  Coeficiente = c("Intercept", "TOC", "Oxygen", "Cu(t-1)"),
  Estimativa = c(4.8837, 0.019764, -0.29578, 0.26096),
  "Standard Error" = c(2.3555, 1.4585e-03, 9.9485e-02, 7.0148e-02),
  "t-value" = c(2.0733, 13.551, -2.9731, 3.7202),
  "p-value" = c("0.03814010 *  🔍","7.8293e-42 ***", "0.00294770 ** ", "0.00019908 *** ")
)

kable(resultados, digits = 6, align = "c", caption = "Generalized Method of Moments Model Results", format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("bordered"),
    full_width = TRUE, 
    position = c("center"),
    font_size = 19, 
    fixed_thead = TRUE) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, color = "gray1") %>%
  column_spec(2, bold = TRUE, color = "gray") %>% 
  column_spec(3, bold = TRUE, color = "gray") %>% 
  column_spec(4, bold = TRUE, color = "gray") %>% 
  column_spec(5, bold = TRUE, color = "gray") %>% 
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#27408B")
```
 
Adjusted Model Equation:

$$
Cu_t = 4.88 + 0.0198 \cdot TOC - 0.296 \cdot O_2 + 0.261 \cdot Cu_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t
$$

## GMM Model Diagnostics: Residual Autocorrelation (Plot)
```{r diagnóstico 3.2, warning=FALSE, echo = FALSE, fig.height=8, fig.width=10, out.width="100%", message=FALSE}
#     🔅 Comportamento dos resíduos:
# Calcule os resíduos manualmente
residuos <- dados_mat[,"Cu_MKF80"] - 
  (coef(modelo_gmm2)[1] + 
     coef(modelo_gmm2)[2] * dados_mat[,"TOC_80"] + 
     coef(modelo_gmm2)[3] * dados_mat[,"O2_80"] +
     coef(modelo_gmm2)[4] * dados_mat[,"Cu_lag2"])

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
acf(residuos, main = "ACF of Residuals", lag.max = 10)  # FAC = Função de Autocorrelação
pacf(residuos, main = "PACF of Residuals", lag.max = 10)  # FACP = Função de Autocorrelação Parcial
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

## GMM Model Diagnostics: Heteroscedasticity (Plot)
```{r diagnóstico 4.2, echo = FALSE, fig.height=8, fig.width=10, out.width="100%", message=FALSE}

test_df <- tibble(
  residuos = residuos,
  TOC_80 = dados_mat[,"TOC_80"],
  O2_80 = dados_mat[,"O2_80"],
  Cu_lag2 = dados_mat[,"Cu_lag2"],
  fitted = 
    coef(modelo_gmm2)[1] +
    coef(modelo_gmm2)[2] * dados_mat[,"TOC_80"] + 
    coef(modelo_gmm2)[3] * dados_mat[,"O2_80"] +
    coef(modelo_gmm2)[4] * dados_mat[,"Cu_lag2"]
)

# 2. Teste BP modificado
bp_test <- bptest(residuos$Cu_MKF80 ~ TOC_80$TOC_80 + O2_80$O2_80 + Cu_lag2$Cu_lag2 +
                    I(TOC_80$TOC_80^2) + I(O2_80$O2_80^2) + (Cu_lag2$Cu_lag2^2) + 
                    fitted$TOC, data = test_df)

# Gráficos dos resíduos combinados
# Gráfico de dispersão CORRETO para resíduos vs valores ajustados
p1 <- ggplot(test_df, aes(x = fitted$TOC_80, y = residuos$Cu_MKF80)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "blue") +
  labs(x = "Fitted Values", y = "Residuals") +
  theme_minimal()

# Gráfico de resíduos vs valores ajustados (corrigido)
p2 <- ggplot(test_df, aes(x = fitted$TOC_80, y = residuos$Cu_MKF80)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.6, color = "skyblue3") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#D55E00") +
  labs(
    title = "Residuals vs Fitted Values",
    x = "Fitted Values", 
    y = "Residuals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Histograma CORRETO dos resíduos
p3 <- ggplot(test_df, aes(x = residuos$Cu_MKF80)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),  # Eixo y em densidade
    bins = 10,                     # Número de barras
    fill = "skyblue",              # Preenchimento azul
    color = "black",                 # Contorno vermelho
    linewidth = 0.5                 # Espessura da linha
  ) +
  geom_density(color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +  # Linha de densidade
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Residuals with Red Outline",
    x = "Residuals",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# QQ-Plot
p4 <- ggplot(test_df, aes(sample = residuos$Cu_MKF80)) +
  stat_qq(size = 2.5,color = "skyblue3") +
  stat_qq_line(color = "blue4")+
  labs(title = "QQ-Plot dos Resíduos")

# 2. Combinar os gráficos CORRETAMENTE
combined_plot <- p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 # Usando o operador + do patchwork

# 3. Visualizar o resultado
combined_plot + 
  plot_layout(ncol = 2)  # Organiza em 2 colunas

```

## Impact of Doubling (2x) Oxygen in the System
```{r impacto-03, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
# 1. Criar dataframe com todas as variáveis necessárias
dados_plot <- mkf7 %>%
  select(Data, Cu_MKF80, TOC_80, O2_80) %>%
  mutate(
    # Criar a variável Cu_lag (lag de 1 período)
    Cu_lag = lag(Cu_MKF80, 1),
        # Calcular as previsões para ambos os cenários
    Cu_normal = coef(modelo_gmm2)[1] + 
      coef(modelo_gmm2)[2] * TOC_80 + 
      coef(modelo_gmm2)[3] * O2_80 + 
      coef(modelo_gmm2)[4] * Cu_lag,
    
    Cu_O2_dobrado = coef(modelo_gmm2)[1] + 
      coef(modelo_gmm2)[2] * TOC_80 + 
      coef(modelo_gmm2)[3] * (O2_80 * 2) + 
      coef(modelo_gmm2)[4] * Cu_lag
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Cu_lag))  # Remover NA da primeira observação

# 2. Gráfico comparativo CORRETO
ggplot(dados_plot, aes(x = Data)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Cu_normal, color = "Measured O2"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Cu_O2_dobrado, color = "Elevated O2"), linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(y = Cu_MKF80, color = "Observed Cu"), size = 2) +
  geom_text(aes(y = Cu_MKF80, label = round(Cu_MKF80, 1)),
            vjust = -1, size = 2, color = "orange4") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Measured O2" = "blue", 
                                "Elevated O2" = "red", 
                                "Observed Cu" = "black")) +
  labs(title = "Copper Behavior with Measured vs. Elevated Oxygen",
       subtitle = paste("Oxygen Effect: coefficient =", round(coef(modelo_gmm2)[3], 4), 
                        "| Expected reduction when doubling Oxygen =", 
                        round(mean(dados_plot$Cu_normal - dados_plot$Cu_O2_dobrado, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "ppb"),
       x = "Date",
       y = "Copper Concentration (ppb)",
       color = "Scenario") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",  
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
```

## Impulse Response Function: Impacts of O2 and TOC on Cu
```{r VAR, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, out.width="100%"}

library(vars)
library(tidyverse)
library(tseries)

# 👉 Converter para séries temporais:
# Para seus dados COM GAPS (datas faltantes):
# Especificar explicitamente o pacote
# Método 2: Pipeline completo com tratamento robusto
mkf6_clean <- mkf6 %>%
  dplyr::select(Cu_MKF80, O2_80, TOC_80) %>%
  na.omit()  # Remove linhas com qualquer NA

# Converter para série temporal
mkf6_ts <- ts(mkf6_clean, start = 1, frequency = 1)

# Diferenciar
mkf6_diff <- diff(mkf6_ts)

# Verificar se não há NAs
print("Verificação de NAs:")
print(colSums(is.na(mkf6_diff)))

# Agora executar VAR
var_selection <- VARselect(mkf6_diff, lag.max = 10, type = "const")
print(var_selection)

# $selection
# AIC(n)  HQ(n)  SC(n) FPE(n) 
#  3      2      1      3 

# Para inferência/ Interpretação (mais foco na parcimônia). Assim:

# 👉 Use SC/BIC (sugere 1 lag) - modelo mais simples
var_model <- VAR(mkf6_diff, p = 2, type = "const")
summary(var_model)

# 2. Analisar função impulso-resposta
irf_results <- irf(var_model, n.ahead = 5, cumulative = TRUE)
plot(irf_results)

# 3. Decomposição da variância
fevd_results <- fevd(var_model, n.ahead = 5)
plot(fevd_results)

# 4. Testar se precisa remover variáveis não significativas
var_model_simplified <- restrict(var_model, method = "ser", thresh = 1.0)
summary(var_model_simplified)
irf_results2 <- irf(var_model_simplified, n.ahead = 10, cumulative = TRUE)
plot(irf_results2)

# Estimation results for equation Cu_MKF80: 
#  ========================================= 
#  Cu_MKF80 = Cu_MKF80.l1 + O2_80.l1 + TOC_80.l1 + O2_80.l2 

# Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
# Cu_MKF80.l1 -0.529031   0.113755  -4.651 1.61e-05 ***
#  O2_80.l1    -0.161505   0.087954  -1.836 0.070757 .  
# TOC_80.l1    0.024459   0.006538   3.741 0.000383 ***
#  O2_80.l2    -0.148814   0.087745  -1.696 0.094533 .  
# ---
#  Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1


# Residual standard error: 6.93 on 67 degrees of freedom
# Multiple R-Squared: 0.297,	Adjusted R-squared: 0.255 
# F-statistic: 7.075 on 4 and 67 DF,  p-value: 8.186e-05 

# Plot personalizado apenas para as relações do Cobre
# Criar o layout PRIMEIRO
# Calcular IRFs individuais

# Calcular IRFs individuais
irf_o2_to_cu <- irf(var_model, impulse = "O2_80", response = "Cu_MKF80", 
                    n.ahead = 6, cumulative = TRUE)

irf_toc_to_cu <- irf(var_model, impulse = "TOC_80", response = "Cu_MKF80",
                     n.ahead = 6, cumulative = TRUE)

# Agora plotar com layout
par(mfrow = c(2, 1))

plot(irf_o2_to_cu, main = "Impact of Oxygen on Copper")
plot(irf_toc_to_cu, main = "Impact of TOC on Copper")

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# Function to convert irf to dataframe
irf_to_df <- function(irf_obj, impulse_name) {
  n_ahead <- length(irf_obj$irf[[1]]) - 1
  data.frame(
    horizon = 0:n_ahead,
    effect = as.numeric(irf_obj$irf[[1]]),
    lower = as.numeric(irf_obj$Lower[[1]]),
    upper = as.numeric(irf_obj$Upper[[1]]),
    impulse = impulse_name
  )
}

# Convert irf objects
df_o2 <- irf_to_df(irf_o2_to_cu, "Oxygen")
df_toc <- irf_to_df(irf_toc_to_cu, "TOC")

# Create ggplot plots
p1 <- ggplot(df_o2, aes(x = horizon, y = effect)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.3, fill = "blue") +
  geom_line(color = "darkblue", size = 1) +
  labs(title = "VAR: Impact of Oxygen on Copper",
       x = "Time Horizon", y = "Effect on Copper") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(df_toc, aes(x = horizon, y = effect)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.3, fill = "red") +
  geom_line(color = "darkred", size = 1) +
  labs(title = "VAR: Impact of TOC on Copper",
       x = "Time Horizon", y = "Effect on Copper") +
  theme_minimal()

# Combine with patchwork
p1 / p2  # One above the other



```

```{r Teste da hipótese de O2, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
  ) +
  
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(
      shape = c(16, 17, 15),
      linetype = c("solid", "solid", "solid")
    ))
  ) +
  
  labs(title = "Behavior of Copper, Oxygen, and TOC During the Study Period") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Conclusion {.build}

 ✔️ The track removal process in the Generator should be `standardized`;

 
 ✔️ The `Copper` concentration in the system has strong temporal dependence;


 ✔️ The `GMM` model with one lag proved to be robust ("J-test" with p-value = 0.92);


 🔍 To reduce the `Copper` concentration in the system, it is recommended to reduce `TOC` and increase the `Oxygen` concentration. That is:
 
     ✅  1. Using the A1 water inventory, via F. & B., control the TOC value;
     
     ✅  2. By Instructing the Shift Team, adjust O₂ to 25-30 ppb range.
